title: Outlook for Mac: agents in Copilot Chat
summary: The briefing passes: the roadmap facts, control paths, commands and licensing statements are supported. It correctly distinguishes included agents from pay-as-you-go agents and qualifies availability management for tenants not yet migrated to unified app management.

claims.where: title; summary; What's changing; rationale: risk
claims.claim: This item adds declarative agent support to Copilot Chat in Outlook for Mac.
claims.quote: We will be adding declarative agents support in Copilot Chat in Outlook. This roadmap item tracks availability in Outlook for Mac.

claims.claim: The roadmap gives no preview date.

claims.claim: The roadmap record was modified at 2026-10-08T23:04:12.
Declarative agents configure Copilot for scenarios by adding custom instructions, knowledge and actions.
claims.quote: Declarative agents enable you to configure Copilot for specific scenarios by adding custom instructions, additional knowledge, and actions to automate business processes.

claims.claim: Microsoft Learn lists Outlook among the Microsoft 365 apps where declarative agents run.
claims.quote: Channels: Run in Microsoft 365 Copilot and Microsoft 365 apps like Teams, Word, Excel, and Outlook.

claims.claim: Copilot Chat users can discover and use agents from the chat experience.
claims.quote: Copilot Chat users can discover and use agents from the chat UX.

claims.claim: Agent access can be controlled and configured in the Microsoft 365 admin center.
claims.quote: Control and configure access to agents within the Microsoft 365 admin center.

claims.claim: Declarative agents can use custom knowledge from Microsoft 365 data sources and Copilot connectors.
claims.quote: Custom knowledge to connect Microsoft 365 data sources (such as Teams messages, Copilot connectors, SharePoint, and OneDrive) or external data via Microsoft 365 Copilot connectors.

claims.claim: Declarative agents can include custom actions that integrate with APIs to interact with external systems.
claims.quote: Custom actions to integrate with APIs to interact with external systems in real-time.

claims.claim: No Microsoft Learn page specifically describing this Mac agent-support item was found as of November 2026.
claims.quote: Searched: "Outlook for Mac" "agents" "Copilot Chat" 486696; "486696" "declarative agents" "Outlook" "Mac". Opened agents-overview, manage-agents-copilot-chat and Microsoft 365 Copilot release-notes; no feature-specific Mac page found.

claims.claim: The Copilot release notes document integrated declarative-agent extensibility for classic Outlook for Windows under roadmap ID 481559.
claims.quote: We added integrated extensibility experience support for declarative agents in Copilot Chat in Outlook. This release note covers availability in classic Outlook for Windows. Roadmap ID: 481559

claims.claim: The cited Copilot release notes have no entry for roadmap ID 486696.
claims.quote: Searched: fetched https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/copilot/release-notes for 486696, 481559 and Mac/declarative-agent combinations. Found Windows item 481559 twice and no 486696.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; Why it matters; Open questions
claims.claim: Included declarative agents are available by default subject to existing Teams and Microsoft 365 app store settings, supporting defaultState on.
claims.quote: These agents are available by default and are found in the store based on your existing store settings for Teams and Microsoft 365 apps.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.model and notes; Scope
claims.claim: The licensing model is mixed, with included agents and consumption billing depending on the user's licence and agent grounding.
claims.quote: Declarative agents that are grounded in instructions and public websites are included with Copilot Chat (Basic), and Microsoft 365 Copilot (Basic) and (Premium). Access to agents that use shared tenant data are pay-as-you-go only.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Instruction- and public-website-grounded declarative agents are included with Copilot Chat (Basic) and Microsoft 365 Copilot (Basic) and (Premium).
claims.quote: Declarative agents that are grounded in instructions and public websites are included with Copilot Chat (Basic), and Microsoft 365 Copilot (Basic) and (Premium).

claims.claim: Agent use comes with the Microsoft 365 Copilot (Premium) licence.
claims.quote: No action is needed to enable agents for Microsoft 365 Copilot (Premium). The use of agents comes with Microsoft 365 Copilot (Premium) license.

claims.where: Cost and licensing; Risk assessment: Data exposure; rationale: cost
claims.claim: For Basic licences, agents accessing shared tenant data such as SharePoint or Graph Connector content are billed based on metered consumption.
claims.quote: For Copilot Chat (Basic) and Microsoft 365 (Basic) licenses, agents that access shared tenant data, such as SharePoint or Graph Connector content, are billed based on metered consumption.

claims.claim: The documented pay-as-you-go agent setup requires a new or existing Copilot Studio subscription.
claims.quote: You must set up or use an existing Copilot Studio subscription.

claims.where: Why it matters; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: Pay-as-you-go agents are off by default for Copilot Chat (Basic) and Microsoft 365 Copilot (Basic) users.
claims.quote: Pay-as-you-go agents are turned off by default for Copilot Chat (Basic) and Microsoft 365 Copilot (Basic) users

claims.claim: A pay-as-you-go billing policy budget triggers email notifications.
claims.quote: When you set a budget amount, it triggers email notifications based on your organization's spending relative to that limit.

claims.claim: A billing policy budget does not enforce a spending cap or stop usage.
claims.quote: However, the system doesn't enforce the budget or prevent your organization from exceeding it. Usage can continue uninterrupted even after the budget is surpassed, ensuring no disruption to the service.

claims.where: controls[0].note; Cost and licensing; Governance controls
claims.claim: Access to the Package Management API requires a Microsoft Agent 365 licence.
claims.quote: Access to the Package Management API requires a Microsoft Agent 365 license.

claims.claim: The documented Graph block operation is a beta preview API.
claims.quote: Block (preview) | POST /copilot/admin/catalog/packages/{id}/block | Block a package to prevent its usage.

claims.claim: The documented beta block API is not supported in production applications.
claims.quote: APIs under the /beta version are subject to change. Use of these APIs in production applications is not supported.

claims.where: controls[0].ui; Governance guidance; Governance controls table
claims.claim: The block control is reached through Microsoft 365 admin center > Agents > All agents > agent > Block.
claims.quote: Select Agents > All agents. In the All agents page, select an agent from the list of agents. In the agent details pane that opens, immediately under the agent's name, select Block or Unblock.

claims.claim: POST /beta/copilot/admin/catalog/packages/{id}/block blocks a Copilot package to prevent its use.
claims.quote: Block a Copilot package to prevent its usage. POST https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/copilot/admin/catalog/packages/{id}/block

claims.where: controls[0].governs and scope; Risk assessment; Governance controls
claims.claim: The agent block control restricts access across the whole organisation.
claims.quote: Block and unblock | Restrict access to an agent across the organization, preventing any user from using it.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance controls
claims.claim: Blocking Agent Builder or Copilot Studio agents affects availability and functionality in Copilot and other hosts including Outlook.
claims.quote: Blocking or unblocking an agent that you created by using Microsoft Copilot Agent Builder and Microsoft Copilot Studio affects its availability and functionality in Microsoft Copilot. It also affects availability and functionality in other host products, such as Microsoft Outlook

claims.claim: Blocking a SharePoint or Microsoft Foundry agent only affects its availability in Copilot Chat.
claims.quote: However, blocking an agent that you created by using SharePoint or Microsoft Foundry only impacts its availability in Microsoft Copilot Chat.

claims.claim: The printed Teams admin center path through Teams apps, Manage apps, the app, Users and groups, Availability and Edit availability reaches Available to.
claims.quote: Select the Users and groups tab. Under Select to manage who this app is installed for or available to in your organization, select Availability. Select Edit availability. Select the required option from Available to menu.

claims.claim: Update-M365TeamsApp -Id <app id> -AppAssignmentType Everyone is a MicrosoftTeams cmdlet call that sets the app's availability to Everyone.
claims.quote:
Update-M365TeamsApp -Id 4c4ec2e8-4a2c-4bce-8d8f-00fc664a4e5b -AppAssignmentType Everyone
Updates the availability value for Bookings app (App ID 4c4ec2e8-4a2c-4bce-8d8f-00fc664a4e5b) to Everyone.

claims.claim: App centric management lets administrators assign users or groups per app or Copilot agent to control who can add and use it.
claims.quote: This functionality lets you specify which users and groups can use each app or a copilot agent and you can control it on a per-app basis. To allow users to add and use an app or a Copilot agent, you must assign users or groups to an app.

claims.where: controls[1].note; Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance
claims.claim: App availability changes, including UI and PowerShell changes, can take up to 24 hours to apply.
claims.quote: UI or PowerShell changes take up to 24 hours to apply to all users, consistent with anytime UI or PowerShell updates occur, not just immediately after migration completion.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: In rare cases availability changes can take up to six days to appear in the client.
claims.quote: It takes up to 24 hours for the availability changes to take effect. In rare cases, it might take up to six days for the changes to reflect in the client.

claims.claim: Before unified app management migration, apps and Copilot agents must be allowed in both Teams admin center and Microsoft 365 admin center Integrated apps.
claims.quote: If your organization isn't migrated to unified app management, allow apps and Copilot agents in Teams admin center and under the Integrated apps page in Microsoft 365 admin center.

claims.claim: After unified app management migration, either Teams admin center or Microsoft 365 admin center Integrated apps can manage availability.
claims.quote: If your organization is migrated to unified app management, allow apps and Copilot agents in Teams admin center or under the Integrated apps page in Microsoft 365 admin center.

claims.claim: The Update-M365TeamsApp reference describes the cmdlet as updating the Microsoft Teams app.
claims.quote: This cmdlet updates app state and app available values for the Microsoft Teams app.

claims.where: Why it matters; Scope; Governance controls
claims.claim: Unified app management synchronises availability between the admin centres and governs availability across Teams, Outlook and Microsoft Copilot apps.
claims.quote: After your tenant is unified, all changes to org-wide settings, agent app, status, or availability in TAC are automatically synchronized in MAC and vice versa. Ensures org-wide defaults for both admin centers are in sync and governs app availability across Teams, Outlook, and Microsoft Copilot apps

claims.claim: The roadmap record specifies no feature-specific licence or price.
claims.quote: We will be adding declarative agents support in Copilot Chat in Outlook. This roadmap item tracks availability in Outlook for Mac.
